translations.text: And the Lord says: “For three acts of lawlessness by Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away from it, because they cut apart the pregnant women of Gilead with iron saws.”
“And I took some of your sons to be prophets and some of your young men to be Nazirites. Is this not so, children of Israel?” says the Lord.
“Therefore, behold, I will roll beneath you, just as a wagon full of sheaves rolls.”
“The archer shall not be able to stand his ground, the swift-footed shall not escape, and the horseman shall not save his own life.”
Can a trumpet be sounded in a city without the people being alarmed? Can disaster occur in a city without the Lord having brought it about?
“And I inflicted [?] toothache in all your cities and a lack of bread in all your places, yet you did not return to me,” says the Lord.

“I struck you with scorching heat and inflicted [?] blight. You multiplied your gardens, vineyards, fig trees, and olive trees, but the caterpillar ate them. Even so, you did not return to me,” says the Lord.
“Do not seek Bethel, do not enter Gilgal, and do not go up to the Well of the Oath, for Gilgal shall surely be taken captive, and Bethel shall become as though it had never existed.”
If you hate evil and love good, establish justice at your gates, so that the Lord God may have mercy on the remnant of Joseph.
“I hate and reject your festivals, and I will not savor your annual celebrations.”
This is what the Lord God showed me: behold, a man stood upon a wall of adamant, with a piece of adamant in his hand.
For this is what Amos says: “Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be taken captive from its land.”
The Lord swears by the pride of Jacob: “None of your deeds shall ever be forgotten.”
And the Lord God Almighty, who approaches the earth and shakes it—all its inhabitants shall mourn, and its end shall rise like a river and sink like the river of Egypt.
